previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 45-year-old man with advanced HIV/AIDS and recent history of toxoplasmosis and respiratory failure was admitted from a rehabilitation facility with fever, tachypnea, and altered mental status. He was found to have ventilator-associated pneumonia caused by Pseudomonas aeruginosa, confirmed by sputum and urine cultures, and was treated with cefepime. His respiratory status improved, and he was successfully weaned from mechanical ventilation to trach mask support. Treatment for ongoing cerebral toxoplasmosis was continued, with MRI showing stable lesions and reduced edema. Thrush was treated with fluconazole, and CMV/HSV pneumonia prophylaxis was maintained with valganciclovir. His hospital course was complicated by transient hyponatremia and bladder outlet obstruction, both managed conservatively. He was discharged to extended care with plans for follow-up in infectious disease and neurology clinics.
problems: Pseudomonas infection in conditions classified elsewhere and of unspecified site
Herpes simplex without mention of complication
Other dependence on machines, supplemental oxygen

radiology_notes.text:
REASON FOR EXAMINATION:  Evaluation of the patient with respiratory failure.

AP radiograph of the chest was compared to ___.

The tracheostomy tip is 5 cm above the carina.  Feeding tube is projecting
over the left upper quadrant.  Diffuse ground-glass opacities are covering the
entire chest, overall with no substantial change since the prior examination. 
Differential diagnosis is broad and might include infectious etiology as well
as chronic process.  For precise details and discussion, please review chest
CT that was obtained in ___ and the corresponding report.  Left
internal jugular line tip terminates below the cavoatrial junction and should
be pulled back.

HISTORY:  Admitted with likely sepsis.  Evaluate for obstruction or other
intraabdominal process.

COMPARISON:  CT abdomen/pelvis from ___.

FINDINGS:

Portable upright and supine abdominal radiographs demonstrate a normal bowel
gas pattern without dilated loops of bowel or air-fluid levels to suggest
ileus or obstruction.  There is no pneumatosis or intraperitoneal free air.  A
PEG tube is noted.  There are degenerative changes of the visualized osseous
structures.

IMPRESSION:

Normal bowel gas pattern without evidence of ileus or obstruction, and no
pneumatosis or intraperitoneal free air.

REASON FOR EXAMINATION:  Evaluation of the patient with HIV infection and
pneumonia.

As compared to the prior study, the current AP radiograph demonstrates overall
improvement of the opacities of the lung that might reflect interval
resolution of edema.  Still present are diffuse ground-glass opacities.  The
tracheostomy and the left internal jugular line tip are unchanged in position,
and the left internal jugular line should be pulled back approximately 2 cm.

HISTORY:  Patient with history of AIDS, pneumonia, history of toxo, now more
distended, evaluate for change in toxo lesions, rule out bleed, CVA.  

COMPARISON:  NECT of the head on ___ and MRI head from ___. 


TECHNIQUE:  Contiguous axial MDCT images were obtained through the brain
without administration of IV contrast.  Reformatted coronal and sagittal and
thin section bone algorithm-reconstructed images were acquired.  

CTDI vol:  106 mGy, DLP:  1560 mGy-cm

FINDINGS:

Study is limited by motion.  There are foci of hyperdensity within the left
basal ganglia at the site of known toxoplasmosis lesion, which may be due to
mineralization or a small amount of hemorrhage, without significant local mass
effect.  There is no shift of normally midline structures.  Hypodensities in
the left parietal, temporal, and right frontal regions are unchanged.  No
acute large vascular territorial infarction is identified.  The ventricles are
unchanged in size.  

No fracture is identified.  The visualized paranasal sinuses, mastoid air
cells, and middle ear cavities are clear.  The globes are unremarkable.  

IMPRESSION:

Small foci of hyperdensity within the left basal ganglia at the site of known
toxoplasmosis lesion may be secondary to mineralization or small amount of
hemorrhage.  No shift of normally midline structures.  No acute large vascular
territory infarction.

INDICATION:  Patient with complicated medical history including HIV and
multiple bouts of complicated pneumonia, now with new change in mental status.
Evaluate.

COMPARISON:  ___ CT chest from ___ and ___ as well
as chest radiograph from ___.

TECHNIQUE:  Axial helical MDCT images were obtained through the chest without
administration of IV contrast.  Coronal, sagittal, and axial MIP reformats
were generated in an independent workstation.

DLP:  636.17 mGy-cm.

FINDINGS:

SUPPORT AND MONITORING DEVICES:  An endotracheal tube ends approximately 4.5
cm above the carina.  A central line ends at the cavoatrial junction.  A
percutaneous jejunostomy tube is seen coursing through the small bowel in the
left upper flank with the tip out of view.

LUNGS AND AIRWAYS:  There is diffuse and global increased background density
of the lungs particularly in the upper lobes and interstitial abnormality with
both peripheral and peribronchovascular distribution, particularly at the lung
bases. Small subpleural foci of fibrosis are seen in the posterior portion of
the lungs (representative images 4:90).  However, compared with prior exam,
there has been significant interval improvement of the ground-glass opacities
and diffuse diffuse interstitial thickening suggesting resolution of pulmonary
edema.  There is no new focus of consolidation to suggest pneumonia.  No
pleural effusion is identified.  

MEDIASTINUM:  Numerous scattered mediastinal lymph nodes are not enlarged by
CT size criteria.  Increased caliber of the right pulmonary artery up to 3.0
cm suggests pulmonary hypertension.  The left pulmonary artery is also
prominent.  The aorta is normal in caliber.  The heart is not enlarged and
there is no coronary artery calcification.  Relative hypodensity of the blood
pool with respect to the myocardium is compatible with anemia.  There is no
pericardial effusion.  No hiatal hernia.

This study is not tailored for assessment of subdiaphragmatic structures, and
limited by the lack of IV contrast.  Allowing for these limitations, multiple
calcified gallstones are again seen but there is no evidence of cholecystitis.
Otherwise, the imaged abdominal organs are unremarkable.

OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:  There are no lytic or blastic lesions concerning for
malignancy.

IMPRESSION:
1.  Compared with ___, there has been significant interval
improvement in degree of ground-glass opacities and interstitial thickening,
compatible with improved pulmonary edema.  No new focal consolidation to
suggest infection.  The global and chronic, diffuse, background changes of the
lung parenchyma are stable.

2.  Support devices in appropriate position.

AP CHEST, 4:15 A.M., ___

HISTORY:  ___ man with HIV infection and pneumonia.

IMPRESSION:  AP chest compared to ___:

Diffuse interstitial pulmonary abnormality is improving.  The combination of
diffuse ground-glass opacification and peripheral coarse interstitial
abnormality suggests acute involvement and chronic residua of pneumocystis
infection whereas the relatively acute improvement may have been an overlay of
volume or cardiac-related edema.

Left internal jugular line ends in the right atrium.  Tracheostomy tube in
standard placement.  No pneumothorax or large pleural effusion.

INDICATION:  Evaluation for PICC line.

COMPARISON:  ___.

FINDINGS:  As compared to the previous radiograph, the patient has received a
right-sided PICC line.  The line seems to deviate into the brachiocephalic
vein.  On a subsequent radiograph (from 11:28 a.m. on the same day), the
catheter was brought into correct position.

INDICATION:  Acute on chronic hypoxemia, PICC line placement.

COMPARISON:  ___.

FINDINGS:  The right PICC line now shows a normal course, the tip of the line
projects over the mid SVC.  There is no evidence of complications.  The left
internal jugular vein catheter has been removed in the interval.  No other
change.

CHEST RADIOGRAPH

INDICATION:  Recent PICC line placement.  Evaluation.

COMPARISON:  ___.

FINDINGS:  As compared to the previous radiograph, no relevant change is seen.
The PICC line is in constant position, with the tip projecting over the mid to
lower SVC.  Minimal unchanged opacities at both lung bases.  Unchanged
position of the tracheostomy tube, unchanged size of the cardiac silhouette.

BRAIN MRI WITH AND WITHOUT CONTRAST, ___

INDICATION:  ___ man with AIDS, history of toxoplasmosis, now with
respiratory failure and altered mental status.  Evaluate for change in
toxoplasmosis lesions, cerebrovascular accident, encephalitis.

COMPARISON:  ___ brain MRI with and without contrast.

TECHNIQUE:  Sagittal T1-weighted and axial T1-weighted, T2-weighted, FLAIR,
gradient echo, and diffusion-weighted images of the brain were obtained. 
Following intravenous gadolinium administration, multiplanar T1-weighted
images of the brain were obtained.

FINDINGS:  This study is moderately limited by motion artifacts.  However,
most of the previously noted rim-enhancing lesions with slow diffusion,
consistent with the known toxoplasmosis, have decreased in size.  This
includes the right frontal subcortical lesion on image 11:19, left basal
ganglia lesion on image 11:12, left superior posterior temporal lesion on
image 11:12, left lateral temporal lesion on images 11:9 and 11:8, and a
smaller lesion at the junction of the left temporal and occipital lobes on
image 11:8.  Stable tiny lesions are present in the right basal ganglia on
image 11:13 and in the superior subcortical left frontal lobe on image 11:22. 
No new enhancing lesions are seen.  While FLAIR images are significantly
degraded by motion artifacts, the extent of white matter signal abnormalities
associated with the above-described lesions are stable.

There are no new diffusion abnormalities to indicate acute infarction.  There
is no evidence of new parenchymal edema or enhancement to suggest
encephalitis.  Moderate ventriculomegaly with superimposed ex vacuo dilatation
of the right lateral ventricle is unchanged.  Prominence of the sylvian
fissures and some of the cerebral sulci is also unchanged.  These findings
likely related to cerebral atrophy in the setting of AIDS.  Scattered foci of
high T2 signal in the deep and subcortical white matter of the cerebral
hemispheres, not related to the toxoplasmosis lesions, are stable and may
represent sequela of chronic small vessel ischemic disease.  Similar findings
are also present in the pons, unchanged.

IMPRESSION:
1.  Motion-limited study.  

2.  Continued improvement in intracranial toxoplasmosis without evidence of
new lesions.

3.  No acute infarction.

4.  No evidence for encephalitis.

HISTORY:  Pain.

FINDINGS:  There is a distracted intertrochanteric fracture on the right.

There are also areas of sclerosis involving the femoral heads bilaterally,
raising the possibility of avascular necrosis.

Information about the fracture, which was detected at 9:38 a.m. on ___, was
reported by telephone one minute later to the nurse caring for the patient in
the ICU.

HISTORY:  ORIF.

FINDINGS:  Images from the operating suite show placement of a fixation device
about the intertrochanteric fracture of the right femur.  Further information
can be gathered from the operative report.

INDICATION:  Femoral neck fracture, now with two weeks status post im nailing,
assess for hardware placement and bone healing.

TECHNIQUE:  AP pelvis and two additional views of the right hip.

COMPARISON:  Right hip radiographs ___.

FINDINGS:

There has been prior placement of an intramedullary nail and interlocking
screw into the femoral head and neck.  A minimally displaced intertrochanteric
fracture is still visualized.  There is minimal callus formation.  No
periprosthetic fracture or loosening seen.  There is irregular sclerosis of
the femoral head, raising possibility for avascular necrosis, this is
unchanged compared to the prior study.  Similar appearance in the left femoral
head, also unchanged compared to the prior study.  No concerning lytic or
sclerotic bone lesion is seen.  Unremarkable bowel gas distribution.

IMPRESSION:  Minimally displaced fracture through the intertrochanteric right
proximal femur remains visualized with minimal callus formation.  No hardware
complication seen.  Possible avascular necrosis of the bilateral femoral
heads.

microbiology.comments: NEGATIVE FOR LEGIONELLA SEROGROUP 1 ANTIGEN.            (Reference Range-Negative).  Performed by Immunochromogenic assay.  A negative result does not rule out infection due to other L. pneumophila serogroups or other Legionella species. Furthermore, in infected patients the excretion of antigen in urine may vary.

10-25 PMNs and >10 epithelial cells/100X field.  Gram stain indicates extensive contamination with upper respiratory secretions. Bacterial culture results are invalid.  PLEASE SUBMIT ANOTHER SPECIMEN.

CRYPTOCOCCAL ANTIGEN NOT DETECTED.            (Reference Range-Negative).  Test performed by Lateral Flow Assay.  A negative serum does not rule out localized or disseminated cryptococcal infection.  Appropriate specimens should be sent for culture.

No respiratory viruses isolated.  Culture screened for Adenovirus, Influenza A & B, Parainfluenza type 1,2 & 3, and Respiratory Syncytial Virus.  Detection of viruses other than those listed above will only be performed on specific request. Please call Virology at ___ within 1 week if additional testing is needed.

Negative for Respiratory Viral Antigen.  Specimen screened for: Adeno, Parainfluenza 1, 2, 3, Influenza A, B, and RSV by immunofluorescence.  Refer to respiratory viral culture for further information.
